issues.failure_explanation: The net-extension step bounds the vector difference of the two trimmed embeddings by the sup-norm Lipschitz property of order statistics. But the rows of $\mat{A}^{\vx}$ and $\mat{A}^{\hat\vx}$ are ordered by ABSOLUTE value (signs kept) and the two trimmings keep different index sets; the monotone-rearrangement bound $\|u_{(k)}-v_{(k)}\|\le\|u-v\|_\infty$ does not transfer to abs-sorted signed sequences. Counterexample (m=2, k=0): $u=(c,-c+\epsilon)$, $z=(c-\epsilon,-c)$ with $\|u-z\|_\infty=\epsilon$; abs-sorted vectors are $(-c+\epsilon,c)$ and $(c-\epsilon,-c)$, so the difference has norm $\approx 2\sqrt2\,c$ and $\|\mat{A}^\vx\vx-\mat{A}^{\hat\vx}\hat\vx\|_2^2\approx 8c^2\gg 2\epsilon^2$; the absolute values agree position-wise, so the cited lemma gives zero control on the signed comparison. The correct comparison (order statistics of the squared values, or $g(\vx)=\frac{m}{m-k}\min_{|S|=m-k}\sum_{i\in S}(\va_i^T\vx)^2$) gives $|g(\vx)-g(\hat\vx)|\lesssim m\max_i\|\va_i\|^2\varepsilon\sim n^d\varepsilon$ — first order in $\varepsilon$, not $\varepsilon^2$ — so the net scale $\varepsilon=\delta n^{-d/2}/3$ used in the proof is unjustified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the vector-difference comparison by a comparison of the squared trimmed norms, e.g. via $\big|\min_{|S|=m-k}\sum_{i\in S}(\va_i^T\vx)^2-\min_{|S|=m-k}\sum_{i\in S}(\va_i^T\hat\vx)^2\big|\le\sum_i|(\va_i^T\vx)^2-(\va_i^T\hat\vx)^2|\le 2m\max_i\|\va_i\|^2\varepsilon$ (on the existing event $\mathcal{E}_1$), and take the net at scale $\varepsilon\sim\delta n^{-d}$. The covering logs, and hence the stated sample complexities, survive up to the unspecified constants $C_1,C_2$, so the theorem statements remain intact.
issues.overall_effect: The main trimmed-RIP guarantee of Theorem trim_trip (bounds \eqref{eq:order_m_hosvd}, \eqref{eq:order_m_cp}) is not established by the given argument: the extension from net points to all low-rank tensors fails, so the uniform trimmed geometry-preservation claim over HOSVD/CP low-rank tensors, and its informal restatement in Theorem thm:main-informal, are unproven as written.
issues.title: Invalid order-statistics comparison for abs-sorted trimmed embeddings in the proof of Theorem trim_trip
issues.why_classification: The false step requires a replacement argument (a different inequality and a coarser net scale, changing $\varepsilon$ from $\delta n^{-d/2}$ to $\sim\delta n^{-d}$), i.e. a contained nontrivial repair rather than a routine local edit; however the method, conclusion, probability and sample-complexity order all survive up to constants, with no loss of the advertised regime.

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm sorts the absolute residuals $|\mathcal{A}(\tX^k)-\vb|$ ascending and sets $\Theta_k$ to the first $m_{\text{trim}}$ indices, i.e. it keeps only the $m_{\text{trim}}$ smallest-residual rows and rescales by $m/|\Theta_k|=m/m_{\text{trim}}$. But Definition def:trimmed-matrix removes the $k$ largest $|y_i|$ and keeps $m-k$ rows with scaling $\sqrt{m/(m-k)}$, eq:truncated-A scales by $\sqrt{m/(m-m_{\text{trim}})}$ (i.e. $m-m_{\text{trim}}$ rows), and the stated correspondence identifies $\mat{A}_k$ with $\mat{A}_{m_{trim}}^{Vec(\tX^k-\tX^*)}$ — all using the semantics 'remove the $m_{\text{trim}}$ largest'. As written, the algorithm's row set and rescaling contradict eq:truncated-A and the claimed correspondence (which needs the kept set $[i_1,\dots,i_{m-m_{\text{trim}}}]$, matching the theory and experiments where only $\approx\ln(8n)$, or 5–80 of thousands, of rows are trimmed).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the index set to the kept rows, $\Theta_k=[i_1,\dots,i_{m-m_{\text{trim}}}]$ (keep the $m-m_{\text{trim}}$ smallest residuals), so that $|\Theta_k|=m-m_{\text{trim}}$, the factor $m/|\Theta_k|$ matches eq:truncated-A, and $\mat{A}_k=\mat{A}_{m_{trim}}^{Vec(\tX^k-\tX^*)}$ as claimed.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm TrimTIHT as printed computes a different update from the trimmed gradient it defines and analyzes: it does not match Definition def:trimmed-matrix, eq:truncated-A, or the claimed correspondence, so Theorem thm:main_path (stated for the residuals of Algorithm alg:trimtiht with dynamics per eq:truncated-A) does not apply to the algorithm as coded, and the motivating link to the trimming theory is broken.
issues.title: TrimTIHT keeps the wrong row set: Θ_k selects the m_trim smallest-residual rows instead of removing the m_trim largest
issues.why_classification: A single forced one-line correction to the algorithm's index set (the surrounding definition, equation, correspondence claim, theory and experimental parameter ranges all pin down the intended semantics) restores full consistency; no proof, rate, or guarantee changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof derives only the per-iteration recursion $\|\tR^{t+1}\|_F\le\alpha_t\|\tR^t\|_F$, where $\alpha_t$ depends on the iteration-varying quantities $\mu_t,\rho_t,\Delta_t,\xi_t$ (which vary by design, since the trimming and step sizes adapt to the iterate). Iterating yields $\|\tR^{t+1}\|_F\le\prod_{i=0}^{t}\alpha_i\,\|\tR^0\|_F$, not $\alpha_t^{t+1}\|\tR^0\|_F$: e.g. if $\alpha_0=\dots=\alpha_{t-1}=1$ and $\alpha_t=1/2$, the recursion gives only $\|\tR^{t+1}\|\le\tfrac12\|\tR^0\|$ while the statement claims $2^{-(t+1)}\|\tR^0\|$. No hypothesis forces the factors to be constant, and the induction over $t$ is never carried out, so the stated closed form does not follow.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate eq:conv_path as $\|\tR^{t+1}\|_F\le\big(\prod_{i=0}^{t}\alpha_i\big)\|\tR^0\|_F$ (or $\le(\sup_{i\le t}\alpha_i)^{t+1}\|\tR^0\|_F$) with $\alpha_i$ the displayed per-step factor; the per-step conclusions and the exponential-rate interpretation under uniformly bounded factors are preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised global convergence rate for TrimTIHT (eq:conv_path) is not established in the stated power form; only the per-step contraction bound is proven. The surrounding discussion (Remark rem:trimtiht-discussion) is phrased per-step and is unaffected.
issues.title: Theorem main_path claims a (t+1)-power convergence bound but the proof only establishes a one-step recursion with iteration-dependent factors
issues.why_classification: A local restatement of the conclusion (product/sup over iterations instead of the power of the final factor) matches exactly what the proof establishes and preserves every substantive per-step and uniform-rate claim; no new argument or weakening is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The remark asserts that $(\delta,3\vr)$-TensorRIP (with $m_{trim}=0$) implies $|1-\rho_t|<\delta$. But $\rho_t$ is the Rayleigh quotient of $A^TA$ at $u_t=P_{\Omega_t}(A^TA\vr^t)\in\mathrm{span}\{\vr^t,\vr^{t+1}\}$, and each residual $\vr^t=Vec(\tX^t-\tX^*)$ is a difference of two HOSVD-rank-$r$ tensors (rank $\le 2r$ per mode). Hence $u_t$, an arbitrary linear combination of two such residuals, has HOSVD rank up to $4r$ per mode — outside the rank-$\le 3r$ set on which the assumed TensorRIP holds. The RIP control of $\|Au_t\|$, and thus $|1-\rho_t|<\delta$ and the claimed recovery of TIHT convergence guarantees at $3\vr$-RIP with $\delta<0.106$, does not follow (the companion claim $|1-\Delta_t|<\delta$ is fine, since $\vr^t$ has rank $\le 2r$).

issues.why_classification: The fix is a local strengthening of the hypothesis (RIP level $3\vr\to4\vr$, or an explicit factor-2 slack in $\rho_t$) inside a remark, and the form of the conclusion — a per-step TIHT-type contraction under near-RIP — survives essentially unchanged.
